## 10. Authority recovery, operating assurance and privacy

### 10.1 Required authority/fence interface and acknowledged positions

A complete B is a fresh read from the elected current authority, not a cache, replica, earlier RR view, ETag/304 or last-good fallback. Immutable catalog bytes may be cached by full allowlisted digest; policy state/native eligibility may not. B beginning after acknowledged C must see C or later. A B overlapping C may see the earlier complete state subject to the accepted watermark at D. Native changes acknowledged before F must be reflected with unchanged policy revision. Later overlapping native changes are not promised global cancellation.

Select an operational **FencedAuthorityV1** dependency with methods AcquireCurrent(kind), AssertCurrent(session), RecordAcknowledgedPosition(session,position) and RecoverAtLeast(fence). A session names one authority incarnation/election generation and must be rejected after that generation loses authority. The deployment must fence **reads and writes**, including stale processes/in-flight commits, before exposing the new generation. An online lookup of a stale token or a local timestamp lease alone is insufficient.

RecoveryFenceV1 is a closed minimal security record: fence_version=1, authority_id, kind ("sql"|"im"), incarnation, election_generation (uint64 string), minimum_ack_position (native opaque≤512-byte token), scope_checkpoint_sha256, catalog_set_sha256. scope checkpoint commits scope anchors/nonces/revisions/epochs and retired/non-serving state; its backing snapshot must be recoverable, not only its hash. The record is monotonic under the authority's defined position comparison and persisted outside the data backup's stale-restore failure domain. No policy body or denial content is added to a new outcome service.

Before acknowledging a policy commit/read state to a client, ensure its durable authority position is covered by that external minimum-ack fence. A DB commit followed by a failed fence update is an **ambiguous/unacknowledged outcome**, not a successful write to repeat blindly. Recovery may expose only a verified authority at/above all acknowledged positions and all matching scope/catalog state; otherwise remain unavailable. A stale backup missing newer policy/fence state cannot be relabelled fresh by generating new nonce/epoch/authority ID.

This fixes the protocol dependency and acknowledgement order. It does **not** assert an existing deployed FencedAuthorityV1 provider. Operations must identify its actual current-writer routing, election/fencing mechanism, durability domains, credentials/network exclusions, SQL/IM position semantics and recovery implementation. None was supplied or exercised in this run. I-AUTH/E remain; do not invent an external service/repository or perform deployment changes under document authority. If no approved platform can supply it, PjM requests only that evidenced interface expansion or an explicit requirements tradeoff.

### 10.2 Workload and safety accounting

Define I=admitted/attempted invocations, P=physical action attempts (including pages/hops/retries/publications), H=original contributors revalidated per boundary, T=simultaneously active turns, J=uncompacted journal reservations. Count denied and failed attempts, not only successful business requests.

At minimum, policy work scales with I+P; native fact work can scale with (I+P)×ceil((H+1)/32) and up to three refresh rounds, plus metadata/disclosure/history and prerequisite verification. Every protocol/native/policy retry counts against the **aggregate** proof request budget. Every publication/local-read can create another boundary even with zero outbound business HTTP. A 393-operation catalog count says nothing about request cost.

Measure before selecting service assurance:

- component/end-to-end p50/p95/p99, cold/warm catalog and connection paths, F/B latency and each preparation/lock/fsync queue;
- bytes, contributor fan-out/revalidation, full bundle/catalog parsing/canonicalization, manifest/journal growth and checkpoint cost;
- contention, deadlock/timeout/429 amplification, fairness across keys/callers and saturation behavior at the selected hard bounds;
- clean-thread continuity cost, history omissions, renewal/hard deadline and native publication behavior;
- authority fail-stop/recovery/fence restoration and worst observed loss/uncertainty windows.

Existing quotas/timeouts and V-D's 5-rps envelope are constraints, not capacity results. No quota increase, positive caching, weakened native freshness or “eventual” acknowledged recovery is authorized. Owner chooses measurable service/continuity/RTO expectations after bounded evidence. Exceeding the chosen engineering safety profile returns unavailable/omits optional import; do not silently weaken AC.

### 10.3 Per-artifact storage, readers and lifecycle

The following are proposed controls, not capture/retention permission. PjM/Owner must bind actual existing principals and stores before any execution. Role names below express least privilege; they are not proof that those principals already have access.

| Artifact | Proposed readers/store and lifecycle | Security boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Policy bundle + native anchor + revision/epoch/retirement fence | Existing authorized owner/self projection only; backend/operations narrowly scoped recovery access. Encrypted authority store and separately durable recovery checkpoint. Permanent minimum fence lifecycle needs Owner decision. | Self has P only, no owner attribution; no model policy access; no deletion/reset by test expiry |
| Replay HMAC keys, linkable reservations and native stream fences | Ingress/coordinator service identity; narrowly named recovery operator. Encrypted host security store; keys separated from journal; no ordinary log/capture copy. | Retain/compact only after native horizon/fence proof; key rotation preserves needed old verification; saturation stops serving |
| Context manifests, original content, input/cwd/session/derived state | Only admitted isolated worker and host admission path as required. Per-turn scratch; no cross-turn native resume. Delete/quarantine at close under approved retention and content-access controls. | Digest/epoch is not eligibility; raw bodies/identity map are not refusal evidence; late callbacks remain fenced |
| Minimal refusal evidence | correlation/category and only validated revision if expressly approved; no body/identity/rules/arguments/results/tokens. Proposed private bounded diagnostic access to named QA/independent reviewer. | No durable outcome service or new request-log outcome fields; retention requires explicit approval |
| Restricted validation capture/fixture map | Explicitly named Tester/Independent Reviewer and minimum operators; proposed ≤1 MiB/run, encrypted private store, no backup/export, deletion≤24h. Any real identities/content/effects require explicit inclusion. | Test capture expiry is independent from durable security state. Synthetic markers still require approved handling. |

Do not promise “anonymous” replay hashes: they are linkable pseudonymous security state. Backup/deletion/cancellation and recovery controls must cover each artifact separately, including cleanup after failed proof. Raw screenshots/headers/content/identity maps do not belong in Loop comments. The source/catalog design attachment contains pinned source data, no live credential/message capture.

### 10.4 Administration and compatibility flow

D9 remains a single bounded interpretation decision: accept the proposed versioned subresource on existing authenticated administration, or identify an available alternative/explicit constraint change. The routes are absent from the pinned robot router. An API proposal is not an available operation; no editor is introduced.

FE/BE flow is complete authorized read → retain intended edit → exact CAS write → full authorized readback. Conflict keeps the intended edit and refetches; no blind overwrite or implicit migration. Response loss is unknown until reconciled. A later read establishes observed current state, not necessarily which lost request caused it. Saved means server state, never endpoint application.

Preserve existing /settings nullable override/effective/default-source/editable fields, bool/string normalization and documented malformed-boolean fallback; existing /mcp-policy context-mode generation/CAS and DELETE-to-inherit; mention/card/default consumers and special-container rules. New bundle deactivation/reset/activation is §4 only. Strict mode remains strict when stages U; compatible declaration mode never authorizes E. No source value rewrites target/actor/Space/OBO or forced trusted arguments.

D14 retains existing authentication/rate/not-found/creator-only WithStatus handling. Newly registered permission validation/conflict/unavailable semantics use wire HTTP 400 with the established semantic error envelope; do not accidentally add real 409/503 transport behavior. Owner routes use actual human limiter identity; self/facts routes use actual Bot limiter identity. No credential/profile fallback after denial.

### 3.2 Rules and deterministic bytes

Rule fields: rule_id, effect, caller, source; Stage 2 additionally requires capabilities. effect is allow/deny. caller is exactly {kind:uids,uids:[...]} or {kind:all_humans}; source is exactly {kind:refs,refs:[...]} or {kind:all_in_space,conversation_types:[dm,group,thread as explicitly selected]}. Set selectors are nonempty; all selector alternatives are explicit. References are:

~~~json
[
 {"kind":"dm","id":"canonical raw DM"},
 {"kind":"group","id":"canonical group","include_descendants":false},
 {"kind":"thread","id":"canonical native thread"}
]
~~~

Only omitted include_descendants defaults to false, for group references only; canonical output always includes it. Omitted/null/empty caller/source/capabilities, unknown fields/kinds, duplicate IDs/references, unknown catalog entries and wildcard/regex/display-name selectors reject the entire edit. Stage 1 forbids capabilities; Stage 2 capabilities is a nonempty exact-ID set. Reference existence/scope validation is bounded and transaction-aware; inability to validate rejects, not truncates. Current eligibility remains a runtime fact.

Each rule matches the complete key AND caller AND source AND, for Stage 2, capability; alternatives within a selector are OR. No partial-rule cross product. Compute applicability, including the **same explicit descendant predicate for allow and deny**, then any applicable deny wins; otherwise one complete allow is required. Direct thread allow requires verified parent/access, not a parent rule. Parent deny with descendants=false is inapplicable to a thread. Space-wide threads require explicit thread type.

Selected canonicalization **permission-canonical-json-v1**: validate decoded keys and types before map construction; reject duplicate decoded keys (including escaped equivalents), malformed UTF-8, unpaired surrogates, trailing JSON, unknown fields, null required values and numeric coercion. Decode valid escapes to their exact Unicode scalar sequence without normalization. Sort closed ASCII object keys by byte order; emit UTF-8, no BOM/whitespace/final newline, no slash/HTML/U+2028/U+2029 escaping. Escape quote/backslash; control scalars are rejected in contract strings. Sort UID/type/capability sets by unsigned UTF-8 bytes, refs by canonical object bytes, rules by rule_id; reject duplicates before sorting. Array order is otherwise preserved. Emit schema_version as 1, booleans lower-case, revisions/epochs as strings.

bundle_digest = SHA-256 of canonical **P with only bundle_digest omitted**, including key/nonce/revision/epoch/catalog pin and both complete stages. Owner wrapper/attribution/contract, transport fields and signatures are excluded. Set normalization/default filling precedes digest. This is integrity metadata, not authority/freshness/signature proof.

Selected engineering bounds: raw uncompressed mutation 256 KiB; canonical P **including its digest** 256 KiB; owner complete serialized response 384 KiB and fixed descriptor ≤16 KiB; JSON nesting ≤12. 128 rules/stage, 64 caller/source/capability items per rule, 4096 selector references and 1024 capability references across the bundle. Apply counts and byte/scalar limits together, counting supplied entries before duplicate rejection; no truncation. Reject compressed mutation bodies in v1. Catalog artifact reads have a separate 8 MiB ceiling; do not piggyback them or bundles into the existing 16 KiB verify-bot response. These bound work; they are not performance/SLO measurements.

Static serialization vector: group reference with omitted descendants canonicalizes to
~~~json
{"id":"G1","include_descendants":false,"kind":"group"}
~~~
with no final newline; SHA-256 is **fdf32590c58e4dd5c85f8c602fff10422d85afb5c0c9563cb4dd488715a72f14**. This arithmetic is not an executed Go/TypeScript/product test. The shared future corpus must include both projection shapes, default filling, set ordering, escaped duplicate keys, composed/decomposed IDs, UTF-8-byte ordering across BMP/astral scalars (U+E000 before U+10000), controls/surrogates, uint64 extrema and overflow, native byte/scalar boundaries, incompatible old declaration widths, actions, migration pins and all errors.

## 4. Explicit mutation and catalog migration

Both actions use the owner PUT route, authenticated/authorized before private validation detail. The shared expected object is **exactly** scope_incarnation, revision, catalog_version, catalog_digest; all four must match current storage. No client assigns key, revision, epoch, digest, attribution or stage defaults.

### 4.1 Ordinary mutation

Closed request fields: schema_version=1, action="mutate", expected, changes. changes contains 1–2 objects, at most one per stage; order is not precedence.

| Change action | Required/forbidden action fields | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| activate or reactivate | stage; action; explicit rules array (including []); current stage must U | E with supplied rules only |
| replace_rules | stage; action; explicit rules; current E | E with supplied rules |
| delete_rules | stage; action; distinct nonempty rule_ids, all known; current E; rules forbidden | E with those rules removed |
| reset | stage; action only; rules/rule_ids forbidden; U or E | E-empty |
| deactivate | stage; action only; rules/rule_ids forbidden; U or E | U-empty, erased rules |

stage is invocation/capability. Unknown/action-incompatible members reject. Every successful batch, including no-op replacement/repeated deactivation, advances the **single** bundle revision once and changes attribution atomically. The other stage is preserved. Any Stage 1 U→E, including reset from U, increments persistent context_epoch once. E→E reset does not increment the activation epoch; current history/input eligibility still needs revalidation. Delete-last-allow/reset stays E-default-deny. Reactivation never restores erased grants. No bundle DELETE or legacy delete-to-inherit interpretation.

### 4.2 Selected explicit migration action

Closed request fields: schema_version=1, action="migrate_catalog", expected, target_catalog, capability_rules.

~~~json
{
 "schema_version":1,
 "action":"migrate_catalog",
 "expected":{
  "scope_incarnation":"00000000000000000000000000000001",
  "revision":"17",
  "catalog_version":"old-reviewed-catalog",
  "catalog_digest":"64 lowercase hex characters"
 },
 "target_catalog":{
  "catalog_version":"new-reviewed-catalog",
  "catalog_digest":"64 lowercase hex characters"
 },
 "capability_rules":[]
}
~~~

Digest placeholders illustrate the field's type, not valid literal digests or published artifacts. target_catalog has exactly catalog_version/catalog_digest. capability_rules is mandatory and is the **complete intended replacement**, not a rename table/wildcard or an automatic carry-forward. For current capability U it must be []; for E it contains the explicitly intended rules, possibly empty. Stage 1 rules and both U/E states must remain identical; lifecycle/Stage 1 edits use a separate ordinary CAS mutation. Migration preserves context_epoch because it changes no Stage 1 state/rules or policy semantic version.

In one transaction verify the old pin and nonce/revision; require both old and target immutable artifacts available/valid/allowlisted and the same supported permission semantics; validate the entire resulting two-stage bundle and every exact new capability reference; canonicalize/digest; commit one higher revision and attribution. Different semantics require a separately versioned contract, not this action. Removing or broadening IDs does not grant a substitute. Old rules can be mapped only by explicit new rule submission after owner review; neither draft's global/resource/secret names become compatibility aliases.

Unknown/missing target, unsupported old artifact, digest mismatch, changed states/Stage 1 payload, invalid new reference or stale expected pin rejects atomically. If the old artifact is unavailable, restore the authorized immutable artifact first; there is no blind “latest” recovery migration. Lost response requires complete authorized readback and comparison of both stages/pin/revision, not an assumed success or replay. Catalog rollback uses this action at a **new higher revision**, with the old artifact still supported and explicit intended rules. Keep referenced immutable artifacts available; deleting an artifact is not a revocation mechanism.

This closes the missing administration operation in Tester finding 3. It does not make the proposed route available or authorize a release manifest whose dependency closure is incomplete.

## 7. Finite native authority, fact, history and disclosure contract

The finite schema is now selected. Native providers are **not** declared implemented by naming them. This section separates a complete proposed data/interface contract (D) from the exact missing authority (I) and its unexecuted proof (E). octo-server emits native facts, never Stage 1/2 verdicts.

### 7.1 Shared wire grammar and authority descriptor

All fact objects reject duplicate decoded keys, unknown fields, malformed UTF-8/scalars, coercion and unrecognized versions. IDs use §3.1/3.3. Hex request/read/token IDs are 32 lower-case hex; SHA-256 fields are 64 lower-case hex; timestamps are UTC RFC3339Nano. Opaque tokens are nonempty base64url without padding, ≤512 ASCII bytes, not user-selected IDs. No token carries a bearer Bot credential.

The host-only POST /v1/bot/permission-facts/v1?space_id=S authenticates the real supported bf_ Bot, derives Bot UID, checks exact current native scope authority and discloses only its authorized exact-key references. The body is one of these **closed** arms, all with schema_version=1, profile_version=1, request_id:

- resolve: operation="resolve", purpose="admit" or "contributor" or "reply", references=[{delivery_reference}], 1–32 distinct native-issued tokens.
- history_headers: operation="history_headers", source_reference (a previously disclosed canonical source token), cursor (null for first page or native-issued cursor), page_size (integer 1–32). Selection is fixed oldest-to-newest by native immutable sequence within the authorized source; no arbitrary global/source search.
- history_disclosure: operation="history_disclosure", context_id, context_epoch, headers=[{header_reference}], 1–32 distinct references from authorized metadata pages. context_id is the registered 32-hex manifest ID; epoch is canonical uint64 string.

Raw body ≤32 KiB; total metadata response ≤262144 bytes; each result ≤8192 bytes; maximum JSON depth 12. Limits intersect. The host can request a smaller batch but cannot truncate returned identities/predicates. A maximum-sized valid set exceeding the response bound returns unavailable for that bounded operation; it is not silently incomplete.

A successful envelope has common fields exactly schema_version, profile_version, key, request_id, read_id, observed_at, authorities. The resolve and history_disclosure arms additionally have results; the history_headers arm instead has page. No other envelope fields are allowed. key is the exact origin/Bot/Space key. authorities is a sorted nonempty array of AuthorityDescriptor:
~~~text
authority_id: configured ASCII name, 1..64 bytes
kind: "sql" | "im"
incarnation: 32 lower-case hex
position: native canonical opaque base64url, 1..512 bytes
read_nonce: 32 lower-case hex
consistency: "ack_before_read_start"
started_at: UTC timestamp
completed_at: UTC timestamp
~~~
Descriptors are closed. The authority owner defines the position encoding/comparison and durable incarnation fence. A position is not compared lexically or interpreted as a SQL revision. read_nonce binds the actual new read; timestamps are diagnostics, not freshness leases. A descriptor whose authority, incarnation or comparison semantics is unknown is unavailable.

**F contract:** for each required authority, a change acknowledged before that authority's read begins must be reflected; overlapping changes have that native authority's stated linearization allowance. One result uses one coherent snapshot/cut per authority and identifies its cut. SQL and IM have separate descriptor entries. Do not invent a global atomic SQL/IM snapshot, translate wall time into a common position, or claim a read of a stale mirror is authoritative. Required conflicting cross-authority identity/Space/parent evidence yields unavailable. New current reads are required at each §9 boundary.

Each result corresponds one-for-one and in request order to its submitted reference. Closed alternatives:

- unavailable: exactly reference, status="unavailable", reason. reason is one of authority_unavailable, disclosure_unavailable, receipt_unavailable, parent_unavailable, predicate_unsupported, mirror_lag, authority_conflict, expired_reference, budget_exhausted. It contains no asserted false values or unnecessary identity metadata.
- resolved: exactly reference, status="resolved", header, profile, authority_refs, predicates. profile is one of dm_admit_v1, group_admit_v1, thread_admit_v1, dm_contributor_v1, group_contributor_v1, thread_contributor_v1, dm_reply_v1, group_reply_v1, thread_reply_v1, unsupported_principal_v1. authority_refs names only returned descriptor read_nonce values. predicates is a closed object containing **exactly** the applicable atom names in §7.3, all booleans. No omitted applicable atom, null, arbitrary not_applicable or separate negative envelope.

Known unsupported principal is an authoritative header kind plus the corresponding false human/type atom. Unknown principal/recipient/source is unavailable, not a fabricated kind or native negative. A native-owned, authorized check can return a known false predicate; a missing/lagging mirror cannot.

### 7.2 Header, native receipt, history cursor and disclosure permit

A resolved Header has exactly:
~~~text
header_version: 1
header_reference: native-issued opaque token
message_id: positive signed-64 canonical string
source: {kind:"dm"|"group"|"thread",id:native canonical raw ID}
parent_group: null for dm/group, canonical group ID for thread
space_id: canonical Space ID
author_uid: canonical native UID
author_kind: "human"|"user_bot"|"app_bot"|"system"
recipient_bot_uid: canonical verified User Bot UID
native_message_version: native opaque token
payload_sha256: full hash of the native-defined original payload bytes
delivery: {stream_id,stream_incarnation,sequence}
~~~
delivery stream_id is configured ASCII≤128, incarnation 32-hex, sequence canonical uint64 string. Source equality, parent linkage, recipient, author and original Space are native attested facts. Header tokens cryptographically or server-state bind the entire header, origin, entitled Bot and current disclosure policy. The host cannot mint them. A supplied payload tag, dm_space_presence pair, group suffix or current membership is not that attestation. This format is a required new native provider contract; the pinned source does not have it.

For history_headers the operation-specific envelope field is exactly page={source_reference,page_id,items,next_cursor,end,authority_refs}. Each item is either a bounded resolved Header with header_reference or an unavailable reference; **no body, quote, attachment, summary or encrypted payload bytes**. page_id is 32-hex. next_cursor is null iff end=true. A native cursor binds origin/Bot/Space/source, immutable high-water cut, native sequence continuation, page size, disclosure semantic version, authority incarnation and maximum expiry. It is opaque and replay-safe for metadata; replaying a page does not authorize body retrieval. Authority change/invalid cursor gives unavailable, never an implicit new first page or dropped range.

For history_disclosure the results replace Header/predicates with exactly reference,status="resolved",permit,header_reference,context_id,context_epoch,payload_sha256,authority_refs. Each permit is opaque≤512 bytes, recipient-bound, one-use and short-lived (engineering proposal ≤30 seconds). Native authority re-evaluates current read and original-message visibility for both caller and Bot before issuance and again at body access if any intervening native wait can invalidate it. The required **native internal** ReadDisclosedBody(permit,exact_header_reference,recipient,context_id,epoch) consumes the permit before returning those exact payload bytes; it cannot redirect to another message/version. This is a named missing body-read interface, not a claim that adding a token to current content-first sync supplies it. It returns either bounded exact bytes or unavailable/known native refusal, never another payload. Existing body/attachment limits and ACL remain; fact routes themselves return metadata/permits only. A managed history/content sink cannot bypass this interface through ordinary sync/get. Original deliberate new quotes can be new input; automatic quote/backfill expansion still needs the original contributor permits.

Native providers required inside the backend adapter boundary:

- InspectDeliveredHeaderV1(reference,recipient,configured_key) — native immutable source/author/recipient/Space/version evidence without content-first lookup.
- ReadCurrentAccessV1(header,actors,purpose,read_nonce) — coherent current low-level facts/ACL predicates with §7.1 descriptors.
- ListHistoryHeadersV1(source,cursor,page_size,recipient) — metadata-first immutable-cut pages with per-item disclosure authorization.
- IssueHistoryDisclosureV1(headers,actors,context,epoch) and ReadDisclosedBodyV1 — original-message visibility and exact permitted body.
- GetReplayCheckpointV1(stream,recipient) / FenceThroughV1(stream,sequence) — §8 recovery/redelivery authority.

The adapter methods are **proposed interfaces**, not existing native APIs. Their absence is I-FACT/I-REPLAY. Backend/native IM owners must identify the real implementing authority and its ack/freshness semantics. If it cannot be supplied in the three approved repositories, return the exact missing external interface for a bounded scope request. Do not add a new repository/runtime, after-removal policy-reader privilege or invented native ACL by implication.

### 7.3 Complete predicate applicability and native semantic boundaries

The atom dictionary is finite. Every human admit/contributor/reply profile includes:
identity_supported; author_is_human; author_active; author_not_destroyed; bot_user_active; bot_robot_active; bot_creator_eligible; space_active; caller_space_member; bot_space_member; message_source_exact; message_space_exact; message_author_exact; message_recipient_exact; message_version_exact; source_exists.

Account/native eligibility uses the pinned principal conjunction (including app identity exclusion) and real native destroy semantics. author_not_destroyed does not replace the native <>2 versus stricter creation=0 distinction. An unknown value is unavailable.

The special unsupported_principal_v1 profile is permitted only for an authoritative nonhuman native author/kind. It contains exactly identity_supported=false, author_is_human=false, message_source_exact, message_space_exact, message_author_exact, message_recipient_exact, message_version_exact and source_exists; the last six are resolved native booleans. It requires an authenticated current complete bundle and native header/disclosure authority but asks no inapplicable human DM/history predicates. It produces the applicable enforced-stage known-negative result. Unknown author/kind or unverifiable header remains unavailable, not this profile.

Profile-specific atoms:

- dm_admit_v1 adds dm_peer_exact, dm_human_to_bot_relation, dm_bot_to_human_read_relation, dm_human_blocks_bot_clear, dm_bot_blocks_human_clear, caller_current_read, bot_current_read, caller_original_visible, bot_original_visible.

- thread_reply_v1 contains the common atoms plus parent_verified, thread_not_deleted, parent_space_exact, bot_parent_active_member, bot_current_send, bot_external_access.

For group/thread profiles, external access is an explicit native check; if no external restriction applies, the native provider returns true with its native applicability semantics, rather than the endpoint guessing from member type. For DM profiles those atoms are absent by profile, not omitted arbitrarily. Authoritative unsupported principal makes identity_supported/author_is_human false; do not query another human's relation as substitute.

These atoms describe native facts/operations. **caller_current_read, bot_current_read, original_visible and bot_current_send must invoke the native access authority**, with the following finite semantic obligations. They are not permission-policy decisions or a generic “eligible” bit:

- DM human→Bot ingress friendship/creator branch and Bot→human read/send relationship are distinct. Check both directed block settings separately. Preserve the native creator-or-friend versus inbound relation rules; an owner relationship never supplies a Stage 1/2 grant.

**Source evidence and remaining I boundary:** bot_api/db.go:359 supplies the SQL principal precedent; group/db.go:183 supplies an active membership predicate; bot_api/threads.go:21 and thread GetThread supply parent/deletion checks; bot_api/send.go:468, sync.go:25 and webhook/api_datasource.go:115 show directionally different DM paths; message/db.go:29 selects payload and is not the required header API. ### 7.4 Single classification table

## 8. Private launch, control, replay and context

### 8.1 Source-supported launch carrier and selected isolation boundary

The pinned endpoint chain is adapter → ExecutionScope/agent-bridge → Codex SDK → native CLI. Source-present activity events are observations, not synchronous permission gates. Endpoint package-lock pins SDK 0.163.0 and CLI 0.163.0; no floating install is authorized.

The locked SDK's dist/index.d.ts:224 and dist/index.js:164–250/321–400 expose and implement:

- codexPathOverride: explicit executable path.
- env: explicit environment object; when provided, SDK does not inherit process.env.
- config: structured values flattened to --config; an empty nested object emits key={}.
- configOverrides: raw --config strings forwarded unchanged after structured values and before SDK/thread options.
- startThread/runStreamed, with resume appended only when a threadId is supplied.

This is new **S evidence of a usable argv/environment carrier**. It does not establish native table-merge precedence, OS separation, exclusive MCP routing, process cancellation or network isolation. V3 selects the following concrete adapter contract rather than leaving those interfaces unnamed.

**LaunchPlanV1**, private to the trusted host, is a closed record:
plan_id, coordinator_incarnation, turn_id, capsule_id (32-hex); exact configured key/scope nonce/epoch; native_distribution (locked version, platform, archive SRI, executable member); launcher_hash; relay_id/recipient_id; model_workdir; clean_config_digest; allowed_model_provider; deadline; hard resource profile. No Bot token/control credential is included in any worker-readable plan.

At agent-bridge's CodexOptions construction:

- set codexPathOverride to an absolute immutable host launcher whose only behavior is to launch the pinned native member in the approved isolated worker, forwarding SDK argv/stdin/stdout and structured termination exactly.
- set env to an allowlist, not {...process.env}. No Bot token, Octo task/ordinary credential, host-control key, registry signing key, host config path or owner session reaches the worker.
- use a new dedicated CODEX_HOME and working directory for this invocation; no inherited user/project config, AGENTS/skills/session/log/history/memory/cwd files or extra directories. Required fixed instructions are explicitly staged with known provenance.
- use raw configOverrides for the single turn relay MCP table and explicitly disabled network/search/extra integrations. SDK has this raw carrier. Native CLI's actual table replacement/precedence and project-config search must be demonstrated; an unproved mcp_servers={} override is **not** assumed to erase inherited entries.
- startThread only; do not resume a legacy native thread. A new model turn that needs admitted prior content receives the filtered reconstructed manifest, not an old native session path.

**Selected isolation profile for first proof:** Linux x86_64 worker in separate user/mount/PID/network namespaces and cgroup, worker UID distinct from host/coordinator. Drop capabilities after setup; no host /proc, same-UID process inspection, host filesystem/socket/config mounts or arbitrary inherited FDs. Read-only pinned native/relay binaries; writable per-turn scratch only. Egress allowlist is the named model-provider proxy and turn relay, with direct backend/Bot endpoints blocked. The model can call its turn relay but cannot reach the host-control listener or another turn's relay. A random same-UID socket name is insufficient.

The privileged launcher/supervisor and network/mount policy are proposed code/configuration in the **canonical endpoint repository**. No existing OS guarantee is claimed. If the approved environment cannot provide them, stop and present the exact OS interface/host capability need; do not silently launch under the host UID. macOS/Windows and other native distributions remain unverified; this initial Linux proof does not authorize dropping a supported product platform.

Relay data paths:

- stdio: launcher supplies only the private turn relay over inherited anonymous pipes; only framed MCP goes to the worker, never the host-control channel.
- HTTP: expose only a turn-specific authenticated proxy/recipient channel inside the worker's permitted network. Its token authorizes that one registered turn relay, not Bot identity or host control. Bind peer/recipient and capsule; never accept an arbitrary external Bot bearer as host authentication.
- both terminate at the **same PermissionCoordinator** process and exact-key watermark. They cannot start independent per-connection policy engines. A relay crash closes the capsule, not a second unguarded endpoint.

Exclusive native routing is still **E/I-HOST** until the real configuration loading and isolation interfaces are demonstrated. The supported SDK carrier is closed at source level; the native configuration/OS behavior is not fabricated. Bare direct native stdout events do not become a blocking callback.

### 8.2 Finite private host-control protocol

Use a separate mutually authenticated host/coordinator channel unavailable to the worker. Both peers have distinct configured identities and pinned recipient/coordinator incarnation. Messages are length-prefixed canonical JSON, ≤64 KiB, reject duplicate/unknown fields; no model-originated method or arbitrary URL/command.

Every request has exactly control_version=1, request_id (32-hex), session_id (32-hex), method, payload. For non-Hello methods, reply has control_version,request_id,status ("ok"|"refused"|"unavailable"),payload. Authentication/sequence replay is checked before decoding private payload. The Hello bootstrap/probe and its explicit unavailable-envelope exception below take precedence only for Hello; they do not widen generic method replies. An ok payload is exactly the selected method's return record; refused payload is exactly §9.3's version/category/correlation record; unavailable payload is exactly {reason} with the bounded reason enum from §7.1. No raw exception/credential/body is returned. A failed channel cannot use ordinary credentials or another profile.

Closed method/payload arms:

- hello: the complete Hello-specific contract immediately below applies. It overrides only this method's negotiation/probe/outcome/echo rules, including the unavailable session echo; every other method and the framing/capsule/call-action contract in this section is retained.
- register_ingress: exact configured key, native delivery_reference, authenticated stream tuple and source-payload digest. Returns ingress_id; it is unresolved, not an admitted capsule.
- admit: ingress_id and proposed context_id. Coordinator resolves native header/current facts, obtains complete P and evaluates Stage 1 before protected preparation. Returns capsule_id/turn_id/generation or the typed refusal. Reply-only facts are independent.
- bind_context: capsule_id plus complete finite manifest descriptor/hash. Validates original contributor proof and generation; returns context_generation. It never imports already-read unproven content.
- open_relay: capsule_id, recipient_id, transport ("stdio"|"http"), relay_nonce. Returns a one-turn limited channel handle; no host key/Bot credential.
- renew: capsule_id, expected generation and original ingress reference. Requires new native/current bundle proof and valid original registration within the hard lifetime; returns a later lease expiry. It cannot create a new source or extend the hard deadline.
- close: capsule_id and reason ("completed"|"cancelled"|"refused"|"expired"|"worker_failed"); consumes registration, closes relay, joins owned workers, invalidates queued tickets.
- checkpoint: native stream tuple and acknowledged durable checkpoint. Accessible only to the ingress owner; uses §8.3 before journal compaction.

No arbitrary “check permission” RPC issues a reusable bearer allow ticket. F/B and actual D live in the coordinator-owned sink (§9). The host asks it to execute a prepared action bound to a capsule; the model never receives a positive permission decision it can transplant. Cancellation/refusal is a typed handled outcome, not free-text model instruction.

CapsuleV2 is a private closed record with binding_version=2, capsule_id,turn_id,coordinator_incarnation,endpoint_incarnation,recipient_id,key,scope_incarnation,context_epoch,author_uid,author_kind,Header,context_id,context_generation,created_at,lease_expires_at,hard_deadline. All identity fields exactly match native/configured evidence. MAC/signature domain includes the canonical whole record and recipient; key IDs are host-only. Authentic but unresolved IngressRef is not encoded as an invalid capsule.

Each logical call additionally binds call_id,canonical capability,normalized arguments digest. Each action binds attempt_id,action kind,effective target and exact byte digest. All are distinct 32-hex IDs; reused JSON-RPC request IDs do not create another dispatch. A legitimate multiple call/new retry may use the same still-active capsule but must obtain a new checked action. No model argument, global current-caller variable, caller-controlled header or environment declaration supplies source authority.

#### 8.2.1 Complete Hello-specific negotiation and precedence

Architect-selected correction pending review, not I-HOST/I-REPLAY proof. The managed schema root union selects HelloRequest, HelloOkReply and HelloUnavailableReply together with the retained declaration/verification/error records. HelloPayload and HelloSelection are fragment components only, never standalone wire frames. The literal three positive envelopes use that root entry. Unavailable now echoes the validated request session_id as well as request_id; ok echoes request_id and payload.session_id. This is a deliberate completion of v4's correlation contract for comparison by both consumers.

Authenticate the configured channel before any Hello payload is processed. First check bounded framing/deadline, UTF-8, duplicate keys, outer closed envelope keys, control_version=1, method=hello, valid 32-lowercase-hex request_id/session_id and object payload. Malformed framing/JSON/duplicates, missing or invalid IDs, wrong outer keys/method, absent/nonobject payload, failed authentication, or any non-Hello first frame closes without reply. Never invent correlation. A syntactically valid outer Hello with unsupported payload fields/shape/version selection receives a correlated unavailable/predicate_unsupported; supported-shape configured recipient/origin/incarnation conflict receives authority_conflict; unavailable coordinator receives authority_unavailable. Strict supported-frame schema instances and the bounded pre-negotiation envelope probe are different stages; rejecting a supported-frame payload never licenses a guessed ID. Probe is limited to that closed outer envelope and object payload, not arbitrary RPC dispatch. No public refused Hello arm exists. This Hello-specific unavailable envelope has exactly control_version, request_id, session_id, status=unavailable and payload={reason}; the request_id/session_id echo the validated request. It is the explicit exception to the generic non-Hello reply shape, which has no top-level session_id. The supported ok frame remains control_version, request_id, status=ok and payload containing the echoed session_id plus the selected fields. No refused Hello frame is valid.

RecipientID is exactly 1..256 bytes from 0x21 through 0x7e inclusive. Space (0x20), controls and non-ASCII are excluded. Compare exact configured bytes; never trim, case-fold or authenticate with them. One authenticated channel binds one fresh unpredictable host-preselected session for its entire lifetime. Successful selection is exactly managed binding/metadata/identity v2 with configured peer/origin and pinned endpoint/coordinator incarnation. Unknown or conflicting selection aborts. Second Hello, reused session on another channel, later mismatched session, miscorrelated response or refused arm is a protocol failure: close, no rebinding. Wrong configured recipient on a first well-formed Hello instead produces correlated authority_conflict.

Lost reply or any non-ok closes and aborts before managed input/model/tools. Never retransmit Hello on that channel. A later attempt requires a new authenticated channel and fresh request/session IDs; coordinator restart cannot update a host's pinned incarnation automatically. Replay/session reuse state retains the existing bounded retention/saturation contract; do not evict live/replay state to regain availability. No managed-v1, ordinary-credential or alternate-host fallback. Frame/deadline/replay operating bounds and actual channel isolation remain the retained section 8.5 and I-HOST/I-REPLAY/E obligations. No executable validation or runtime result is implied.


### 8.3 Durable replay, crash recovery and compaction

Select a durable ingress consumption journal plus native stream checkpoint, not a guessed TTL. The journal is host-owned and outside worker/config/capture directories. Before native ACK and before any protected work, atomically append/fsync a reservation keyed by:
HMAC(replay_key_version, configured_origin || recipient_bot_uid || native stream_id/incarnation/sequence || native message_id/version || payload digest).
Use length-delimited canonical components, not string concatenation with ambiguous separators. The linkable digest/key material has its own §10 privacy lifecycle.

Journal state transitions are received → reserved → terminal. Only one successful reservation can admit that native delivery; duplicate concurrent receive returns the existing terminal/in-progress disposition without starting another turn. Registering multiple calls within that turn is separate from native delivery deduplication. A crash after reservation but before admission may lose the request; it cannot replay into new work automatically. Crash after possible D preserves possible prior effect, even if output was lost.

The native ACK must be **after durable reservation**. Current socket ACK-before-handler is insufficient. Required native capability: receive a stable stream incarnation/sequence and delay/coordinate ACK, or use a native durable inbox whose atomic consume cursor supplies equivalent authority. This is I-REPLAY; a host-only map cannot create that missing native guarantee.

Recovery opens the journal under exclusive host ownership, verifies checksums/key version, reads the durable native fence and invalidates all old capsules/positive decisions. Reserved/in-progress records become terminal-uncertain; do not resume their model session or resend an action. If journal/key/native checkpoint is missing, corrupt, rolled back or incomparable, stop serving affected streams. No fresh random coordinator ID makes old native deliveries safe.

**Compaction is watermark-based:** native FenceThroughV1 must guarantee no delivery at/below the committed sequence can ever be admitted after reconnect, migration, restore or key rotation. Persist that authenticated stream-incarnation fence durably in a domain that survives the journal/capture cleanup and stale restore. Only then remove terminal individual journal records ≤that checkpoint. Retain previous HMAC verification keys until every record/checkpoint that depends on them has been safely retired. No checkpoint proof means no compaction; hard journal bound then suspends admission.

A proposed 24-hour test environment/capture expiry does **not** reset replay keys, cursor fences, policy nonce/revision anchors or uncertain attempt state. Cleanup must transfer their required minimal fences to the approved durable security-state store or preserve a non-serving terminal namespace. It may delete disposable bodies/captures independently. Any permanent journal/key/fence lifecycle remains O under §14.

### 8.4 Admission, original-content lineage and clean generation

Before a Stage 1 E admission passes, allow only bounded native header/current-policy/fact prerequisites and necessary non-content protocol work. Do not perform profile/roster enrichment, source history/backfill/quote/media fetch, slash/reconciliation commands, model start, working-state insertion or derived queue insertion. Existing trigger tests (mention/mention-free/DM/thread) choose an invocation candidate, never authorize it. Passive chatter has no automatic invocation right.

A fresh per-invocation native thread, directory and input assembly are selected. Every original message/content item has its own Header, author/source, epoch, immutable content version and admission/disclosure proof. A derived summary/file/memory entry inherits the **union** of all original contributors; it cannot keep only the most recent caller. At each protected boundary revalidate the complete contributor set under the current policy/native facts or discard/isolate the dependent state before use. Denying one old contributor during E→E is sufficient to exclude its descendants even if the invoking human remains allowed.

U→E increments persistent epoch; missed E→U→E while disconnected still invalidates all prior legacy manifests/cwd/session/queues. Old native sessions are never retroactively trusted by relabelling their current caller. In-flight already dispatched work is not globally cancelled/rolled back. All subsequent callbacks/queues must pass current generation/binding. A user's newly deliberate quote can be a new invocation; automatic expansion of its original source remains separately protected.

### 8.5 Finite engineering safety profile and cost limits

These are selected **proposed implementation ceilings**, subject to compatibility/conformance and Owner's later operating-assurance decision; they are not measured SLOs. Fail closed or omit optional imports at a bound; never truncate an identity, contributor set or proof.

| Item | Proposed hard bound / exhaustion behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Live capsules per coordinator | 64; queue at most 64 pending admissions; reject excess before protected preparation |
| Turn lifetime / lease | hard 30 minutes; lease 5 minutes, renew only with new proof; monotonic elapsed clock enforces hard lifetime, detected rollback/unknown clock state refuses |
| Bound calls / physical actions | ≤8 concurrent calls per turn, ≤4 active sink attempts per coordinator; no unbounded fan-out |
| Contributor set | ≤256 originals, complete canonical manifest ≤1 MiB; optional history over bound omitted before bodies; indispensable over-bound context refuses |
| History / fact work | ≤10 header pages×32 items per selected history source; fact batches≤32; ≤256 contributors per final boundary; no implied history support beyond these bounded imports |
| Final refresh | ≤3 F/B rounds per action to accommodate newly activated requirements; exhaustion policy_unavailable; no busy loop or stale allow |
| Per-action preparation | ≤16 MiB local immutable input spool; existing smaller operation/upload limits still apply; no protected open before checked local-read action |
| Journal / metadata | ≤64 MiB journal and ≤100,000 uncompacted reservations; whichever first saturates stops new admissions until approved checkpoint compaction; no TTL eviction |
| Cleanup/drain | stop accepting immediately on close; proposed ≤30-second owned-worker drain then quarantine namespace/non-serving; unknown effects remain uncertain |
| Refusal | one ≤2-second original-route attempt; no retry or alternate-route delivery |

The 256-original bound is a full lineage-set bound, not “256 most recent entries.” Stream completion/renewal timing and fairness/availability costs must be measured. Proposed proof V-A's 16-capsule cap does not validate the 64-capsule product ceiling; V-D's 5 requests/s does not establish capacity. §14 adds separate boundary-extension and later workload requests without silently increasing current proof caps.

## 9. Physical dispatch, publication, host actions and refusal

### 9.1 Exact prepared-action and single-send interface

The pinned client.doWithRetry/httpDo/forbidReplay code permits retries below tool admission, including safe GET/no-bytes cases. A NoRetry flag or wrapper around Do is insufficient. Select a coordinator-owned **one-use sink**, not an arbitrary callback that can make multiple requests.

Private typed interfaces, to be implemented in CLI/endpoint:

- PrepareActionV1(BoundCall,declared_profile_node,effective_input) → PreparedAction. This validates targets/forced identity, serializes exact bytes, reserves queues/rate slots, resolves allowed DNS/proxy/TLS targets, prepares immutable spools and connections, and performs all possible waits before final checks. It does not send business request bytes or publish protected data. Any protected preparation/read is itself a declared checked local_read action first.
- PreparedAction is closed: attempt_id,call_id,capsule_id,generation,profile_node,kind,canonical_capability,effective_target,credential_binding,request_sha256,content_sha256,body_length,sink_handle,preparation_generation. Handles are coordinator-owned; the model cannot create/replace them. kind is local_read/http_request/redis_publish/model_publish/native_publish.
- ExecutePreparedV1(prepared) performs the final proof and **owns** D. It returns exactly sent/result_unknown/refused/unavailable with the typed new refusal carried separately from existing execution outcome. “sent” does not mean successful downstream effect.
- AbortPreparedV1 closes the unused sink and erases spool/handles. A prepared handle cannot be reused or serialized as a grant.

Final sequence for every node/physical repetition:

1. Finish all target binding, immutable byte preparation, queues/rate waits, fsync/reservations, connect/TLS/proxy work. A wait/new side-effectful preparation afterward invalidates the tentative proof.
2. Read every required current native/contributor/disclosure fact F with §7 semantics.
3. Begin a **new complete authoritative bundle read B after F**. Validate full key/anchor/nonce/schema/catalog/digest/stages and accept its revision into the shared watermark.
4. If B introduces required facts/lineage checks not present in F, obtain them and begin another new B, bounded by §8.5. A legacy already-contaminated generation cannot be repaired by simply adding a field.
5. Under the coordinator's same key/incarnation critical section, use that one complete P for Stage 1/2, context generation, recipient/effective-request digest and highest accepted revision checks. If a higher P was accepted, use it only after its required F/B cycle; otherwise abort/recheck. Never combine Stage 1 from one response with Stage 2 from another.
6. Atomically consume attempt_id and perform the sink's first actual externally visible action D before releasing that critical section. No arbitrary user callback, await, worker queue or asynchronous “send later” handoff sits between the check and D. If the sink cannot start synchronously, it returns not-started, consumes/aborts the handle and requires a new prepared action/F/B rather than a hidden retry.

All valid complete bundle reads update the watermark at the coordinator's acceptance linearization, not only allowed reads. It is keyed by exact origin/Bot/Space/nonce plus coordinator incarnation, never borrowed across keys. A delayed revision r cannot D after accepted r+1. Restart drops decisions/handles/capsules and recovers only validated persistent fences, not a cached allow.

**HTTP sink:** fresh preconnected HTTP/1.1 channel, exactly one sealed request, no HTTP/2, redirects/auth negotiation/connection pooling/automatic transport retry or 100-continue. TLS/proxy handshake happens in preparation with no business credentials/body. The first business-byte write is a direct owned nonblocking write/writev under the critical section. An EAGAIN/no-start result does not trigger a library replay; a later attempt needs new proof. Partial write or lost response is result_unknown. After D, remaining bytes/response belong to that one in-flight request and do not create a hidden second request; the design promises no rollback/cancellation of it. A page/hop/redirect/resend opens another action and repeats the full sequence. Credential/header forwarding is sealed and SSRF/origin rules remain.

This requires a new transport implementation; it does **not** claim the existing net/http Transport exposes this guarantee. TLS record buffering, syscall behavior and actual receiver count must be proven. If a supported platform cannot supply an owned first-write boundary, report that exact I-SEND interface, not a fabricated successful hook.

**Local/content/publication sinks:** the same one-use transition owns actual protected file open/materialization, insertion into assembled input/memory/derived queue, or release of a result/bytes/URL to the model/host/native channel. A sink performs only its declared action; it cannot open arbitrary second files or publish to another recipient. Any further await/lookup/queue requires a new prepared checked node. Large content already dispatched as a single sealed stream is in-flight; another independent publication/continuation request is a new node. No pre-read mutable file path is accepted in place of the sealed descriptor/content digest.

**Redis issuance sink:** seal the exact existing allowlisted script/keys/arguments, prepare one connection and own the first command write under D. Disable library retry/reconnect replay. Redis execution/response loss is uncertain. URL publication is a separate freshly checked node even if Redis issuance already happened; denying publication does not erase the earlier permitted issuance.

Policy/identity/native-proof prerequisite requests are a private fixed read-only allowlist on the configured authority, bounded and independently authenticated; they do not recursively ask for a model capability. Their failure never supplies positive fallback. They cannot be repurposed into business HTTP, arbitrary metadata/body access or credential fallback. Count them separately in workload/observation caps.

### 9.2 Native host classification and exact boundaries

The private host is not a blanket Stage 2 exemption. The source-present families below retain their existing native ACL/identity constraints.

| Family / source seam | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| socket protocol ACK, ping, bounded verification/header/fact/policy reads | Necessary non-content protocol/prerequisites; ACK ordered after durable reservation; no invocation grant |
| trigger/router mention/DM/thread/mention-free tests | Preliminary candidate selection only; before Stage 1 no enrichment/history/commands/model/derived work |
| group-context, turn-context, history/backfill/quote/media helpers | Protected original-content admission/disclosure and lineage; checked local/input nodes before read/insertion |
| reconciliation/slash commands, direct agent input, model start and queues | Stage 1/current generation before each protected action; cannot run a “harmless command” before admission |
| ordinary original-route answer, streaming chunk, typing/progress/read receipt | Current admitted generation + exact original route + native bot_current_send; any attributable MCP child also needs Stage 2. No parent/DM fallback. A later denied generation stops subsequent publications. |
| one fixed permission refusal | §9.3's narrow control exception, independent safe native route, no arbitrary content/model output |
| cards/api.ts createCardApi/call/fetchImpl | Source-present client includes profile/card reads, send/edit/event/member requests and event ACK. It is not wired in as a new enabled feature. If later used on a protected attributable path, declare exact read/send/publication nodes and gates first; no blanket card exemption. |
| helper-created clients/scripts/fallbacks/uploads/background work | Carry the original BoundCall and declared node through every sink; unclassified protected work stops. Unknown scope does not become independent work. |

The endpoint appendix's O01–O16 inventory remains the minimum receiving-observer inventory. Its source-present direct fetch/helper/secret/transfer clients must be reconciled with the confined plan. No mandatory MCP path may be deleted to make the inventory appear complete.

### 9.3 One typed refusal, private routing and uncertainty

New JSON-RPC error code is **-32007**, message PERMISSION_REFUSED, data exactly {version:1,category,correlation}. correlation is 32 lower-case hex. No identity/rule/source/token/argument/result/retry/outcome fields. Both execute/call_op, discovery/schema/resources and HTTP/stdio carry the same typed application error. Existing statuses/errors remain independent; do not add execute.status="permission_denied".

| Detected required permission condition, in priority order | Fixed host message |
| --- | --- |
| context_untrusted | This request's context could not be verified. Reference: … |
| policy_unavailable | Permissions could not be checked. Try again later. Reference: … |
| invocation_denied | This Agent cannot accept this request here. Reference: … |
| capability_denied | This attempt was blocked before dispatch. Reference: … |

Existing framing/auth/OBO/strict-context errors can stop earlier without being relabelled. An authentic unresolved ingress lookup is unavailable proof, not automatically forged binding. An unreadable complete current bundle is X. Do not inspect extra private data just to discover a higher/lower category after an existing terminal validation.

The host atomically marks the turn/refusal handled and consumes a deduplication key (turn/correlation/original native route) before one delivery attempt. Generic tool-error/timeout/late-success notices consult that handled state and cannot emit a second refusal. The model's decision to echo text is not the control mechanism. Never automatically retry a typed refusal or reinterpret it as transient tool failure.

Delivery requires independently verified original native DM/group/thread route and current reply-only proof. When the required binding is invalid, its untrusted route is not reused; only separately verified native ingress may supply a safe original route. No route/authority means suppression, no fallback to owner DM or parent group. Maximum one proposed ≤2-second attempt; ambiguous delivery is not retried. Refusal content is only the fixed text/reference, with no quoted user content/rules/private reason.

A previously permitted a1 with lost response remains possibly executed/result_unknown. A later denied a2 has zero refused-attempt dispatch/effect; the exact capability text does not claim the entire command/turn had zero effects. Initial Stage 1 denial means zero prohibited admission preparation/input/commands/model/queues/tools. Running-turn Stage 1 denial stops subsequent refused work. No global cancellation, rollback, deletion or hostile-operator/all-external-effects containment is promised. Existing request-only logs gain no outcome service/fields.
